english: Eligibility for AZM
Which children can receive AZM, how to estimate age, and who must not receive it.
In the field — a CDD shows the AZM pack to a mother and her children.
Age eligibility
AZM is given only to healthy children between 1 to 59 months of age.
Children less than one month or older than 59 months are not eligible.
Neonates (less than one month) are not eligible.
A child who is 59 months in round one receives AZM, but is not eligible in the next round.
Why only children 1 to 59 months?
The AZM safety protocol was set for children 1 month and above.
Younger children are more likely to have side effects.
Children 1 to 59 months have the highest risk of severe malaria and other childhood infections.
This age group has the highest death rates from childhood infections.
Side effects are easier to monitor in this age group (1-59 months).
How to find the child's age
Ask to see the child's health card.
Ask the caregiver the age of the child.
Use a calendar of events.
Step — use these signs to estimate the age of a child under 12 months.
Children 1 to 11 months
1 to 2 months: cannot hold head and neck steady when held upright.
Newborn, less than one month: not eligible (marked with a red X).
3 to 4 months: can hold head and neck steady when held upright.
5 to 11 months: can crawl and can sit without help.
From 3 to 11 months, a child can hold head and neck steady, crawl, and sit without help.
Step — a child of 12 to 59 months can stand or walk, but cannot do the two tests marked X.
Child 12 to 59 months
Can stand, walk or run.
CANNOT raise the arm over the head and touch the opposite ear.
CANNOT stand or jump on one foot.
Older than 59 months: not eligible
Older than 59 months: not eligible
A child older than 59 months can raise the arm and touch the opposite ear. They can stand on one leg for 10 secs or jump on one leg. Do not give AZM.

What to do
Advise the caregiver to take the child to the nearest health facility for further evaluation.
Complete the referral form and give it to the caregiver to take to the health facility.
Do not hand over medicine or the card
Do not hand over medicine or the card
Do not give the caregiver the AZM medicine to give later, or the child record card.
Do not give AZM to children with allergy
Do not give AZM to children with allergy
Do NOT give AZM to children who are allergic to AZM or other macrolide antibiotics.
Ask the caregiver
Does the child get sick after taking antibiotic medicines or similar medications?
Has the child taken AZM or similar antibiotics before?
If so, did the child get sick or have reactions such as rashes, swelling or difficulty breathing?
Do not give AZM after recent antibiotics
Do not give AZM after recent antibiotics
Do not give AZM after antibiotics or similar medicine taken in the last 28 days (4 weeks).
Ask the caregiver
Has the child taken any medicine in the last 28 days or 4 weeks?
If yes, what medicine has the child taken in the past one month?
If possible, ask to see the packet to confirm.
Severe acute malnutrition: look and feel
Visible severe wasting
Visible severe wasting: the child looks extremely thin.
The ribs, shoulder blades and bones are very prominent.
The arms and thighs look like "skin and bones", with little or no muscle.
The child's buttocks may look flat or baggy.
Bilateral pitting oedema
Press gently with your thumb on the top of both feet for about 3 seconds.
If a pit remains after you remove the thumb, oedema is present.
This shows the child has Kwashiorkor, a form of SAM.
AZM should not be given to these children
Children from 60 months and older.
Children allergic to AZM or similar antibiotics.
Children who are sick or have fever.
Children who received AZM or other antibiotics in the last one month.
Children who are currently taking AZM or other antibiotics.
Children who cannot swallow.
